proposal.description: The clear-on-qualify restart only happens when a release qualifies; on the edge an assert qualifies the disagreement count is left at ASSERT_CLKS-1
proposal.reason: Suppose an assert qualifies and flag_in drops on the very next clock. The leftover count is already at or past RELEASE_CLKS-1, so flag_out releases after one low clock instead of RELEASE_CLKS clocks.

proposal.description: The flag_out flip compares the disagreement count against the release time for both directions, so the longer assert qualification is forgotten
proposal.reason: When flag_in goes high and stays high while flag_out is low, flag_out asserts after RELEASE_CLKS clocks (200 us) instead of ASSERT_CLKS (1 ms). An assert-going pulse between those two lengths now gets through.

proposal.description: The counter's clear-on-qualify limit is hard-coded to the release time, so during an assert attempt the count restarts every RELEASE_CLKS clocks and never reaches the assert target
proposal.reason: Once flag_out has released, a flag_in that holds high for any length of time never makes flag_out assert again, because the count is cleared at RELEASE_CLKS-1 before it reaches ASSERT_CLKS-1. Releases still qualify normally.

proposal.description: The flip rule is written for the assert direction only (flag_in high while flag_out low), so a qualified release never updates flag_out
proposal.reason: With RESET_VALUE=1, flag_out comes out of reset high and stays high however long flag_in holds low. The supervisor therefore never sees the fault clear.
